task.title: Regular Firmware Updates
task.shortdesc: Check for and install approved firmware updates for the . Firmware updates can correct software problems, improve device compatibility, and provide security corrections.

prereq.p: Before you install a firmware update, make sure that:

ul.li: The router has a stable power connection.
A computer is connected to the router through an Ethernet connection when possible.
You have the credentials for the .
You have permission to update the router firmware.
The current network configuration operates correctly.
You have created a current backup of the router configuration.

prereq.note: Install the firmware update when a temporary network interruption has the least effect on users.
Do not turn off the router or disconnect its power supply during the firmware update.
Install only firmware intended for and the applicable .

context.p: Firmware controls the operation of the . An approved firmware update can contain security corrections, software corrections, and compatibility improvements.
The firmware version used in this guide is . The version available for installation can be different.
context.note: Use the automatic update function in the when this function is available. Do not install firmware from an unknown website or unauthorized source.
Review the firmware release information, supported hardware, known limitations, configuration changes, and recovery requirements before you approve the update.

step.cmd: Verify that the network operates correctly.

substep.cmd: Confirm that an authorized client device can connect to .
Confirm that the client device can access Internet services.
Confirm that the required wired, guest, IoT, access-point, and mesh connections operate correctly.

info.note: Correct known network problems before you install the firmware update. This action makes post-update problems easier to identify.

step.stepresult: The current network condition is recorded before the firmware update.

step.cmd: Back up the router configuration.

info.p: Export the current configuration and store the backup file in a secure location.
For more information, see .
info.note: Do not continue until you confirm that the backup file was created.

step.cmd: Open a supported web browser on the connected computer.
Go to .
step.stepresult: The sign-in page for the opens.

step.cmd: Sign in to the .

substep.cmd: Enter in the user name field.

step.cmd: Record the current firmware and hardware information.

info.p: Record the following information:

ul.li: The date and time of the update

info.note: Do not record passwords or other confidential credentials.

step.cmd: Open the firmware update settings.

info.p: The firmware update settings can appear under Administration, System, Maintenance, or the .
info.note: Menu and control names can differ by .

step.cmd: Check for an available firmware update.

info.p: Select Check for Updates or the applicable update control.
If the router cannot check automatically, get the approved firmware from the .
info.note: Do not download or install firmware from an unauthorized source.

step.cmd: Verify that the firmware update is compatible.

info.p: Confirm that the update applies to:
info.note: An incompatible firmware file can prevent the router from operating correctly.
Confirm whether the update requires an intermediate firmware version, a configuration conversion, or a specific installation sequence.

step.cmd: Review the firmware release information.

info.p: Review the following information when available:
info.note: Determine whether the update affects wireless security, DHCP, DNS, access control, mesh operation, guest access, or IoT network isolation.

step.cmd: Download the approved firmware file if a manual update is required.

info.p: Save the firmware file to a secure local folder on the connected computer.
Do not rename, modify, or extract the firmware file unless the update instructions require that action.
info.note: Verify the file name, version, product model, and hardware version before you continue.

step.cmd: Verify the firmware file integrity if required.

info.p: Compare the file checksum or digital signature with the information supplied on the approved download page.
info.note: A matching checksum helps confirm that the file did not change during download. A checksum does not by itself confirm that the source is authorized.

step.cmd: Start the firmware update.

choices.choice: For an automatic update, select Update or Install.
For a manual update, select the approved firmware file and then select Upload or Install.

info.p: Confirm the update when the requests confirmation.
info.note: Do not turn off the router, disconnect the power supply, close the update page, or disconnect the update computer while the firmware is transferred.

step.cmd: Wait for the firmware update to complete.

info.p: The can restart automatically during the update.
Network access is not available while the router restarts.
info.note: Do not use the router until the status indicators show normal operation.

step.stepresult: The router completes the firmware update and restarts.

step.cmd: Reconnect the computer to the router.

choices.choice: Reconnect the Ethernet cable if the wired connection does not reconnect automatically.
Connect to if you use a wireless connection.

step.cmd: Sign in to the after the router restarts.
Verify the installed firmware version.

info.p: Open the router information or system information page. Confirm that the displayed firmware version matches the installed update.
Record the new firmware version in the maintenance record.

step.stepresult: The router shows the expected firmware version.

step.cmd: Verify the router configuration.

info.p: Confirm that:

ul.li: The guest network settings are correct.
Access-control and device-isolation settings are correct.
Access points and mesh nodes are online.

info.note: Do not assume that all custom settings remain unchanged after an update. Review important settings before you return the network to normal use.

step.cmd: Verify client-device connections.

substep.cmd: Connect an authorized wireless device to .
Connect an authorized wired device to the network.
Confirm that both devices can access Internet services.
Confirm that the devices appear on the .

step.stepresult: Authorized wired and wireless devices can access the local network and Internet services.

step.cmd: Verify the guest network if the guest network is enabled.

substep.cmd: Confirm that the test device can access Internet services.
Confirm that the test device cannot access the primary network or the .

step.stepresult: The guest network operates and remains isolated from the primary network.

step.cmd: Verify IoT, access-point, and mesh connections.

info.p: Confirm that required IoT devices, the , and the are online.
Test the approved functions of selected IoT devices.
info.note: Confirm that IoT isolation, mesh backhaul, access-point channel settings, and applicable access-control rules operate as expected.

step.cmd: Monitor the network after the firmware update.

info.p: Check the network for unexpected disconnections, performance changes, or device compatibility problems.
info.note: Review available system events for restarts, authentication failures, WAN link changes, DHCP failures, access-point disconnections, and mesh-node disconnections.

step.cmd: Update the firmware maintenance record.

info.p: Record the following information:

ul.li: The product model and hardware version
The verification tests that were completed

info.note: Do not record passwords, backup passwords, access tokens, private keys, or other confidential credentials.

step.cmd: Sign out of the .

info.p: Close the browser if you used a shared computer.

result.p: The uses the approved firmware version. The router configuration and required network connections operate correctly.

postreq.p: After you install the firmware update:

ul.li: Monitor network operation for unexpected changes.
Create a new configuration backup after you confirm stable operation.
Store the backup and maintenance record in secure locations.
Check for subsequent firmware notices regularly.

postreq.p: If the router does not operate correctly after the update, record the displayed status indicators and error messages. Contact the through an approved support channel.
postreq.note: Do not perform a factory reset unless the approved support instructions require this action.
Do not send passwords, access tokens, private keys, backup files, or other confidential information to technical support unless an approved secure process specifically requires the information.
